title: docmeta AI-context vocabulary (1.0.0-proposal.1)
description: How machines made and may use this page: production provenance (`generated-by`, `provenance`) and consumption guidance (`risks`, `sample-questions`). The provenance pattern is the family's human-review loop — machines propose, entries retire as humans review — and `risks` uses the open-enum idiom: recommended flags anchored in published prior art, any string legal, unknown values read as caution rather than absence.

generated-by.description: The model, agent, or tool that generated this page's content, if any. Consumers use it for self-preference-bias checks: a judge should know when it is grading its own author.

provenance.description: Attribution for machine-proposed frontmatter, one entry per model (consumers merge by generated-by; the schema dedupes identical entries): which fields it proposed, at what confidence. The human-review trail for enrichment — a human deletes an entry once its fields are reviewed, so a surviving entry means unreviewed machine metadata. Complementary to `generated-by`, which attributes the page's content rather than its metadata.

risks.description: Flags for what following this page does, each a pre-flight question for an agent or reviewer. Cautions: `cost-incurring` (spends money), `destructive` (changes or deletes existing state), `irreversible` (cannot be undone), `privileged` (needs elevated permissions), `open-world` (reaches external systems beyond your control). Assurances: `read-only` (changes nothing) and `idempotent` (safe to repeat) — worth stating explicitly, because an unannotated page is unassessed, not safe. The last three mirror MCP's tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint), the published prior art for agent-facing hints. All seven are recommendations, not a closed list: any non-empty string is legal, and a consumer switching on a flag should treat an unknown value as caution rather than absence.

sample-questions.description: One question, or a list of them, that a reader would ask that this page should answer — `How do I install the operator on EKS?`. The retrieval-eval hook: ask them against the corpus and measure whether this page carries the answer. Assertion-style per-page evals belong to docmeta:evals:1.0.0-proposal.1, not here.

generated-by.description: Model or agent that proposed the fields.

fields.description: Which frontmatter keys it proposed. Unenumerated, unlike kg's self-referential list — the fillable surface here extends across every schema stacked on the page.

provenanceEntry.description: One model's proposal: who generated it, which of these keys it wrote, and how sure it was. Closed, because the whole value of the trail is that a reviewer can read it at a glance and delete the entry once the fields are checked — an unrecognized key here would be an unretired claim nobody notices.

riskFlag.description: One risk flag: a recommended value, or any non-empty string. The enum branch is advisory — it feeds editor completion, docs, and fill proposals; the open string branch keeps an org-specific flag a correct document rather than a violation.
